A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bidirectional predictive coding work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, generation, representation-learning, XOR, bimodal-learning, and missing-input experiments, with numerical results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds linear decoding, stochastic distribution learning, parameter-count controls, and deep-network experiments.

M1.justification: The original energy function and local weight updates remain, but v2 adds stochastic posterior inference and Monte Carlo learning for distribution estimation (Section 3 and Appendix A.5). Appendix I also introduces error-reparameterized optimization and staged generative/bidirectional inference for deep models. These extend the actual training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny-ImageNet and extends missing-pixel evaluation to CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet (Section 4.6). Section 4.2 additionally evaluates unsupervised distribution learning and unconditional sampling, extending v1's reconstruction and label-conditioned generation tasks.

E2.justification: A VAE is newly evaluated against the PC models for MNIST distribution learning (Section 4.2, Table 13). The existing comparison methods remain; arbitrary-graph PC, shared-weight bPC, and activity-decay discPC were already evaluated in v1 Appendix C.

E3.justification: New protocols include linear classifiers trained on representations, separate tuning for decoding and FID, stochastic training with 50 or 250 inference steps, and enlarged baselines matched to bPC's parameter count. The deep-network experiments introduce additional architectures, preprocessing, normalization, and a 1,000-plus-2,000-step inference schedule. These are additions alongside the retained original protocols.

E4.justification: New Appendix G tests whether the original advantages survive matching parameter counts. v2 also adds representation-decoding analysis, compares distribution learning at two inference budgets, and tests missing-input robustness in deeper networks. The earlier energy-weighting sensitivity study and max-pooling ablation remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds independent-samples t-tests with n=5 and p<0.05, marking comparisons significantly worse than bPC in Tables 10–12 and 14–15. Corresponding original results already reported five-seed means and SEMs. Figure captions now identify those error bars explicitly; this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: The numerical values in v1 Tables 10–16 are retained in v2 Tables 10, 11, and 14–18. Substantial new results appear for decoding, distribution learning, parameter-count controls, and deep-network robustness. Examples include bPC's MNIST FID of 3.34±0.53 with 250 activity updates (Table 13) and 73.4% CIFAR-10 accuracy with 50% missing pixels (Figure 8, Table 26), under newly introduced settings.

T1.justification: v2 adds a mathematical specification of independent Gaussian inference noise and second-order Langevin updates (Equation 4 and Appendix A.5, Equations 7–8). The original energy and learning equations remain. The hybridPC objective in Appendix H is relocated from v1's main text, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about biologically plausible bidirectional inference and combined generative/discriminative performance. The introduction refocuses the energy-landscape contribution from OOD detection toward capturing the training distribution and qualifies the multimodal contribution as learning in a bimodal architecture.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 refines the efficiency argument: bPC halves value neurons while retaining the same error-neuron count, with added discussion of dendritic error computation. Appendix H adds an interpretation of bottom-up learning as inversion supporting amortized inference. The central mutual-regularization explanation and max-pooling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents stochastic updates, ancestral sampling, linear readouts, parameter-matched layer widths, and deep-model architectures, preprocessing, optimizers, schedules, and inference settings (Appendices A.5, G, and I). These substantially expand reproducibility information. The future code-release promise remains, but v1's GitHub organization link is removed.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially broaden the biological and computational positioning. New discussion covers sampling-based perception, additional biologically motivated bidirectional models, and a machine-learning subsection addressing U-Net, VAVAE, VAR, and PredNet. The new scaling procedure is also positioned relative to error optimization.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and much of the experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Section headings become descriptive claims, Section 4.5 gains named subsections, and the hybridPC explanation moves into an expanded Appendix H. These changes reorganize and clarify existing material beyond simply appending new experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains explicit error-propagation arrows, Figure 4 expands with decoding and distribution-learning panels, and new Figures 8 and 13 display deep-network results and reconstructions. New result and implementation tables accompany these additions. Retained figures are resized or rearranged, captions are expanded, and the document's typography and layout are reformatted.

improvement.justification: Appendix G directly addresses the parameter-count confound in the original MNIST/Fashion-MNIST comparisons. Expanded representation and distribution evaluations in Section 4.2 and deep-network tests in Section 4.6 materially strengthen the evidence for usefulness and generality. Added statistical tests and implementation details improve assessability. Remaining reporting weaknesses, including unlabeled paired accuracies in Tables 24–26 and removal of the planned code-location link, are limited relative to these gains.
